content.text: Looking up phase band gaps so I can justify the measurements. Cu-rich vanadates look most promising at 2.06 eV illumination. First up: a Cu₃V₂O₈-like composition.

input.verdict: Supportive, but only indirectly. MEGNet HSE gaps: Fe2O3 2.77 eV and V2O5 2.83 eV, both above the 2.06 eV photon energy, so Fe- or V-rich end members should absorb poorly. CuO is 0.32 eV, too small a gap with poor transport. Cu vanadates such as Cu3V2O8 (gap about 1.8-2.0 eV by literature) sit between these, so the Cu-rich/V region near Cu:V 3:2 with a little Fe (index 131) is a reasonable first probe.

The Cu-rich point 131 gave 1.4e-7 A. As a second probe I am testing the CuV2O6-like region (Cu:V about 1:2, low Fe), where the literature gap is about 1.9 eV and falls below the photon energy.

input.verdict: Weakly cautionary. The model gives CuO a near-zero gap (PBE 0.04 eV), so pushing too far toward Cu-rich risks CuO-dominated, recombination-limited films. However, the measured merit already rose from the CuV2O6-like region (5e-8 A) to the Cu-rich region (1.4e-7 A), and the GP UCB also picks 203. Index 203 (Cu 0.63, V 0.24) is a modest extrapolation along that trend, still in the Cu-vanadate/Cu5V2O10-like range rather than pure CuO, so I am proceeding.

content.text:
I submitted index 203 (Cu 0.63, Fe 0.14, V 0.24) as the best composition. At 2.1e‑7 A it had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured. I can't say how close that is to the best in the library, because I only sampled 3 of 296 compositions.

| Index | Composition (Cu / Fe / V) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 50 | 0.26 / 0.09 / 0.65 | 5.0e‑8 A |
| 131 | 0.56 / 0.12 / 0.31 | 1.4e‑7 A |
| 203 | 0.63 / 0.14 / 0.24 | 2.1e‑7 A |

- **Why Cu-rich:** photocurrent went up with Cu content in all three measurements. That fits the idea that copper vanadates can absorb at the 2.06 eV (602 nm) illumination. The band-gap model predicts Fe₂O₃ and V₂O₅ at about 2.8 eV, too wide to absorb at that energy, so I left the Fe-rich and V-rich regions out.
- **How the first pick was made:** with no data yet, index 131 was a judgement call from memory of the literature on copper vanadates, not a model result. The model's "suggest next sample" tool only became useful after the third measurement, when it agreed on index 203.
- **Model evidence was thin:** the phase list was too long to read with the tools I had, so I couldn't look up phase IDs. I guessed IDs for only three simple oxides (Fe₂O₃, V₂O₅, CuO), and the model knew all three. I have no stability or band-gap results for any Cu–Fe–V mixed phase.
- **Not tested:**
  - The trend may keep rising at even higher Cu. The model gives CuO a near-zero gap, so there is probably a limit somewhere, but I couldn't measure beyond 203 to find it.
  - I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so I don't know which crystal phases are actually in these films.
